description.current: Wellington is New Zealand's capital, a compact city wrapped around a harbour and climbing steep green hills. Te Papa, the national museum, sits on the waterfront beside cafés, galleries and a lively food scene. A cable car, a wildlife sanctuary and film studios round out what is easily the most walkable city in the country.
description.proposed: Wellington has been New Zealand's capital since 1865. Limited land between harbour and hills keeps the centre dense, and the Golden Mile from the railway station to Courtenay Place is easy to walk. Beyond the main sights, Weta Workshop runs tours of its film-effects studio in Miramar, and Cuba Street is the bohemian strip of cafés, bars and live music.
alternates: Wellington has been New Zealand's capital since 1865, and its centre is dense because there is so little flat land between the harbour and the hills. The Golden Mile, from the railway station to Courtenay Place, is easy to walk end to end. Day trips go by ferry to Matiu/Somes Island or Days Bay, or by road to the seal coast at Red Rocks.

The capital since 1865, Wellington is a harbour city with little room to spread, so its centre is compact and walkable. The Golden Mile runs from the railway station to Courtenay Place. Film fans can tour Weta Workshop, and the Wellington Writers Walk sets 23 writers' quotes into the waterfront path.
